newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees higher interest rates, weaker peso.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees higher interest rates, weaker peso.

text.p: Philippine finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Wednesday he expected a slight rise in interest rates and some weakening in the peso as a result of the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
"I see slightly higher interest rates and slightly higher exchange rate ... towards depreciation," de Ocampo told reporters at a news conference.
De Ocampo said any impact from the devaluation of the Thai baht would be short-term.
De Ocampo's statements came in response to queries at a news conference scheduled ahead of the Thai developments.
The news conference was called to give details of the Philippines' budget surplus and the status of its IMF programme.
Earlier today, soon after Thailand effectively devalued the baht, the Philippine Central Bank raised interest rates and sold hundreds of millions of dollars to shield its own currency.
It increased its one-day reverse repo rate twice during the morning to 24 percent, up from 15 percent when the paper was last offered three weeks ago.
Traders estimated the Bank also sold up to $500 million.
